rubric.why: Identifies how work is calculated and the direction condition.
rubric.description: Work is the product of force and distance moved in the direction of the force.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the product of force and distance, with the direction condition stated.

rubric.why: Identifies the SI unit of work.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for joule or its symbol J.

modelAnswer: Work is defined as the product of magnitude of force and the distance covered in the direction of force. The SI unit of work is joule (J).

rubric.why: States that energy is an ability or capacity.
rubric.description: Energy is the ability or capacity of a body.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying energy as an ability or capacity.

rubric.why: States what the body is able to do.
rubric.description: The body is able to do work.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the ability is to do work.

modelAnswer: Energy can be defined as the ability of a body to do work.

rubric.why: Identifies kinetic energy as energy possessed by a body.
rubric.description: Kinetic energy is energy possessed by a body.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the energy of a body.

rubric.why: Identifies motion as the reason the body possesses this energy.
rubric.description: The body possesses it by virtue of its motion.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the energy is due to motion.

modelAnswer: The kinetic energy of a body is the energy that a body possesses by virtue of its motion.

rubric.why: Identifies potential energy as energy possessed by a body.
rubric.description: Potential energy is energy possessed by a body.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the energy possessed by a body.

rubric.why: States that the energy is due to position or deformation.
rubric.description: The body possesses it by virtue of its position or deformation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating either position or deformation.

modelAnswer: Potential energy is defined as the energy that a body possesses by virtue of its position or deformation.

rubric.why: States that energy cannot be created or destroyed.
rubric.description: Energy cannot be created or destroyed.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating both that energy cannot be created and cannot be destroyed.

rubric.why: States that energy may change form while the total remains unchanged.
rubric.description: Energy may be transformed from one form to another, but the total amount remains constant.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that energy transforms between forms and the total amount does not change.

modelAnswer: Energy cannot be created or destroyed. It may be transformed from one form to another, but the total amount of energy never changes.

rubric.why: Defines power as work done per unit time.
rubric.description: Power is the time rate of doing work.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that power is the rate of doing work over time.

rubric.why: Identifies the SI unit of power.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for watt or its symbol W.

modelAnswer: Power is defined as the time rate of doing work. The SI unit of power is watt (W).

rubric.description: Efficiency is a ratio of energies.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the relationship as a ratio.

rubric.why: Identifies useful output energy and total input energy as the quantities in the ratio.
rubric.description: The ratio is useful output energy to total input energy.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for including useful output energy and total input energy.

modelAnswer: The ratio of useful output energy and the total input energy is called the efficiency of a working system.
